summary: WDAC blocks SCCM agent service start after Windows 11 22H2 in-place upgrade causing provisioning/enrollment loop
description:
Issue summary: After performing an in-place upgrade from Windows 11 21H2 -> 22H2 on several Lenovo devices, the SCCM client (ccmexec) fails to start due to WDAC enforcement. Devices repeatedly exit OOBE/provisioning and reapply imaging tasks, resulting in an enrollment/provisioning loop for end users.

Impact: ~24 developer laptops affected across two regions; users unable to complete provisioning or access corporate resources. Timed reboots and repeated autopilot/OOBE restarts observed. Triage escalated because this blocks new hires and several existing engineers.

Environment: Production autopilot-imaging profile; affected devices report as Lenovo models listed above; build image includes SCCM client v5.00.9088.1000 and WDAC policy bundle deployed via ConfigManager baseline.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start with device in OOBE and autopilot profile applied.
2) Apply latest image which performs an in-place 21H2 -> 22H2 upgrade.
3) During first-boot, ConfigManager baseline pushes WDAC policy and attempts to start the SCCM client service ccmexec.
4) Observe service start failure and automatic restart of OOBE/provisioning sequence.

Observed behavior: ccmexec fails to start with exit code 0xC0000409; Windows event logs indicate Device Guard/WDAC blocked the executable due to a hash mismatch. SCCM logs (CcmExec.log) contain repeated "Service start failed: Access denied" and "WDAC enforcement: prevented image execution" entries.

Expected behavior: WDAC policy should allow signed SCCM binaries (company-signed) and SCCM client should start normally so provisioning can complete.

Logs/snippets:
- EventLog (System): "Device Guard: Image execution prevented. Rule type: AllowList, Hash not recognized: C:\Windows\ccm\ccmexec.exe"
- CcmExec.log: "Failed to start ccmexec.exe, error 0xC0000409"
- WDAC audit logs show a policy hash mismatch against the manufacturer-supplied signed list.

Temporary workaround: Reimaging device with a fresh 22H2 offline image that includes the updated WDAC policy manifest resolves the loop. Manual acceptance (audit->permit) of the SCCM binary via local WDAC policy also allows ccmexec to start, but not scalable.

Business risk: High for onboarding cadence. If left unaddressed, new machines may require manual imaging intervention and SRE time for each onboarding.

Request: Investigate why WDAC policy deployed by ConfigManager rejects the company-signed SCCM binary after in-place upgrades. Determine whether the 22H2 upgrade changes file hashes (compression, signatures) or if policy manifests are not being refreshed. Provide a fix path and a short-term mitigation to prevent more devices from entering the loop.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-12: Initial triage - reproduced on two lab T14s. Confirmed ccmexec hash differs from manifest recorded in WDAC policy bundle.

2026-02-13: Compared ccmexec.exe from 21H2 base image vs post-upgrade; observed byte differences despite identical version metadata. Hypothesis: Windows upgrade re-signing/packaging changes binary hash.

2026-02-14: Pulled WDAC policy deployment logs from SCCM. Policy distribution completed, but policy manifest created during initial image build remains unchanged. Possible mismatch between manifest creation time and post-upgrade binary state.
2026-02-15: Confirmed that manual replacement of WDAC manifest with an 'AllowHash' entry for the post-upgrade ccmexec allows service start. This is not a long-term solution.

Next steps: Create reproducible test that captures binary delta during upgrade and verify whether ms-signed signature flag changes. Coordinate with Applied ML infra team for automated policy rebuild and with Build system to include post-upgrade manifest generation in image pipeline.

resolution: Workaround and short-term mitigation: publish an updated WDAC manifest containing post-upgrade hashes for SCCM binaries and roll out to autopilot image distribution. Long-term fix: update image build pipeline to generate WDAC manifests post-upgrade and add a validation step to detect hash drift. Follow-up action: Security to sign and approve the new manifest and SRE to automate manifest generation in CI. Pending tasks: security approval and controlled rollout (planned 2026-02-18).
